title: Oriole implementation scratchbook
content:
Quick personal scratchbook for Kestrel Retail (private deployment) — working notes, decisions, and micro-tasks. Informal; copy important bits to Confluence after validation.

2026-03-03 09:15 — kickoff sync with Kestrel infra (Matt + Lina)
- high-level ask: VPC + on-prem connector; strict egress rules, no public endpoints.
- they want dedicated pool (2x A10G) with burst to 4 during peak. target p99 latency < 120ms for chat flows.
- compliance: logs to customer SIEM via syslog (TLS). retention 90d.

Immediate TODOs
- [ ] open SE-4778 with infra sizing notes + cost estimate (priority)
- [ ] confirm VPC peering IP range w/ Kestrel network (Lina)
- [ ] prepare minimal canary plan: route 5% traffic to new endpoint; automatic fallback to hosted model if pool exhausted
- [ ] draft rollback playbook (sequence + who paged)

Notes from config brainstorm
- autoscale: min=2 workers, target-util=65%, max-burst=4 (burst capacity is paid but needed for day-parting).
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for chat prompts (expect high reuse ~40%). set cache ttl=10m initially.
- quantization: start with int8 dynamic for base layer, hold off on int4 until evals finish.

Command snippets / checks (notes to self)
- check GPU health: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv
- runtime logs: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runtime/req-processor.log
- hook for canary: POST /routes/{route}/rollout {"percentage":5, "fallback":"hosted-redwood-v1"}

2026-03-04 15:45 — customer demo prep
- demo script: show baseline hosted vs private p50/p95; emphasize deterministic routing policies (cost tier + latency).
- show metrics: token-cost breakdown, per-route trace for long conversation (KV hits).
- demo failover: simulate pool OOM -> auto-fallback to hosted. practice the manual rollback steps.

Outstanding questions (need answers before next call)
1) Does Kestrel require HSM integration for key wrapping or is KMS sufficient? (Action: ask security SME Priya)
2) Are there any egress destinations blocked that will impact health checks to Redis? (Action: Lina to confirm)
3) Which model family do they want pinned? they mentioned "open-chat-large-v2" — need OOM profile and perf numbers.

Risk register (quick)
- risk: burst capacity cost exceeds budget if traffic spikes > anticipated — mitigation: add traffic shaping rule and alert on spend burn rate (daily).
- risk: KV cache warming cold start could spike latency for first 30 minutes — mitigation: pre-warm with synthetic runs, warm-up schedule in deployment window.

Implementation micro-plan (day-by-day, rough)
- Day 0: infra prep, VPC peering test, KMS check, basic routing rules in staging
- Day 1: deploy dedicated pool to staging, enable KV cache, run perf suite (p50/p95, memory)
- Day 2: canary deploy to 5% prod traffic, monitor for 4h, check memory, latency, error rates
- Day 3: roll canary to 25% then 100% if metrics green, otherwise rollback + post-mortem

Post-deploy checklist (for SRE handoff)
- [ ] Alerting: GPU temp, OOM, queue length, per-route error > 0.5%
- [ ] Dashboards: cost per 1k tokens, KV hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies
- [ ] Runbook link prepared and tested (link to Confluence placeholder: CONFLUENCE:RDW-priv-deploy-playbooks/kestrel)

Short-term experiments to run in staging
- experiment A: increase batch window to 12ms and measure latency vs tokens/sec for short convo length (<= 128 tokens).
- experiment B: int8 quant + adjusted kernel selection -> check generation quality on prompt set (use Kestrel sample prompts).

Random snippets (to copy later)
- "If canary fails due to OOM, reduce sequence-length cap from 2048 -> 1024 and retry; this reduces KV memory dramatically."
- manual fallback URL: https://api.redwood-inference.internal/fallback-hosted/v1/chat (staging only)

Notes to self: keep this raw. After we've validated the steps with infra and security, formalize into a deployment runbook and push to Confluence.

Recent edits: 2026-03-05 08:10 — added rollback steps and HSM question.

End of scratchbook entry.
